subject: Accounting
title: Lean Accounting
description: A fast breakdown of Lean Accounting for builders.

hook.text: Traditional accounting tracks every labor minute. Lean accounting says: stop counting, start flowing.

buildup.text: Lean accounting supports lean manufacturing—eliminating waste and focusing on value streams.

discovery.text: Instead of tracking individual product costs, it measures the performance of entire value streams.

twist.text: Standard costing can actually encourage overproduction—making more to absorb overhead looks good on paper.

climax.text: Lean accounting aligns financial reporting with operational reality—what actually creates value.

punchline.text: Stop producing waste just to make the numbers look good.

quiz.question: What does lean accounting focus on?

details.summary: Lean accounting adapts management accounting practices to support lean manufacturing principles—eliminating waste, simplifying reporting, and organizing financial data around value streams rather than departments or products.
details.whyItMatters: Traditional accounting methods can actually work against lean initiatives by rewarding overproduction and penalizing underutilization. Lean accounting aligns financial reporting with lean operational goals.
takeaways: Lean accounting organizes costs by value stream rather than by department or product
It eliminates complex overhead allocations in favor of simpler, direct cost tracking
Box scores replace traditional reports with a single-page summary of operational, financial, and capacity metrics

faq.question: What is lean accounting?
faq.answer: Lean accounting redesigns financial reporting to support lean manufacturing principles. It replaces complex departmental cost allocations with value stream costing, simplifies reports, and measures what lean organizations care about: flow, quality, delivery, and waste reduction.

faq.question: Why do lean companies need different accounting methods?
faq.answer: Traditional accounting encourages overproduction (to absorb overhead into inventory), penalizes lean practices (underutilized capacity looks like waste), and requires complex allocations. Lean accounting removes these misaligned incentives by focusing on value stream profitability.
